text_blocks.snippet: In Massachusetts, vaccines are mandatory for school attendance, with exemptions for medical or religious reasons. While Massachusetts law requires vaccinations for school entry, it also allows for exemptions. There is no state mandate for COVID-19 vaccination, but some employers may implement mandates.
snippet_highlighted_words: vaccines are mandatory for school attendance, with exemptions for medical or religious reasons

list.snippet: Massachusetts law mandates that students provide documentation of immunizations before attending school.
Exceptions are allowed for medical or religious reasons.

Medical exemptions must be documented by a physician, while religious exemptions require a written statement from the parent or guardian stating that the vaccine conflicts with their sincerely held religious beliefs.
Required immunizations for school entry include MMR (measles, mumps, and rubella), Tdap (tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis), Varicella (chickenpox), Hepatitis B, and meningitis vaccine.
Massachusetts does not have a state-wide COVID-19 vaccine mandate for the general public, according to state and federal resources.
Some employers may choose to implement COVID-19 vaccine mandates, especially in healthcare settings.
Massachusetts law also requires certain immunizations for college students.
The Massachusetts Immunization Information System (MIIS) (MIIS) is a system that tracks immunization records and helps ensure individuals are up-to-date on recommended vaccines.
There have been efforts to eliminate religious exemptions for school vaccinations in Massachusetts, but these efforts have not been successful.
